title: Cognitive Flexibility Index
shortDescription: Task-switching and rule-reversal exercises measuring how easily you adapt when the rules change mid-task.
longDescription: Cognitive Flexibility Index is a real, live implementation of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (Berg, 1948; Grant & Berg, 1948) — the defining neuropsychological measure of set-shifting. You sort cards under four key cards by a rule (color, shape, or number) that is never stated — you infer it from right/wrong feedback, and once you've found it, it silently shifts to a new rule after 6 consecutive correct sorts. Getting caught applying the old rule after a shift (a "perseverative error") is the classic clinical signal WCST is built to detect.
sourceNote: This is a genuinely live, adaptive implementation of WCST's mechanic, not a static approximation — the correct answer isn't fixed at authoring time, it's a hidden rule the runner tracks and shifts after 6 consecutive correct sorts, exactly like the real test. That required a real interactive component (src/components/questions/WCSTGameQuestion.tsx, a single `custom_interactive` question tagged "wcst") rather than seed content, since the standard question-and-answer runner has no way to give live feedback or branch on prior answers within an assessment. Parameterized after the published WCST-64 short form (64 cards, 4 categories) rather than the full 128-card/6-category version, to keep the session length realistic. The component computes its own normalized 0-1 performance score (category completion weighted 70%, resistance to perseverative errors weighted 30%) and reports it through the engine's generic custom_interactive scoring path (src/lib/scoring/engine.ts) — the same mechanism any future live interactive game would use, not a WCST-specific hack. The genuine published WCST is a commercially distributed clinical instrument (PAR Inc.) with its own card deck and norms; this uses an original 4-color/4-shape/4-count card set implementing the same paradigm.

sections.name: Card Sorting
sections.description: Sort cards under the four key cards by an unstated, shifting rule.
sections.instructions: Watch the feedback after each sort — that's the only way to find (and re-find) the rule.

scoringDimensions.label: Cognitive Flexibility
scoringDimensions.description: Set-shifting ability — finding a hidden sorting rule and adapting when it changes, measured live via category completions and resistance to perseverative errors.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Finding the hidden rule (and re-finding it after a shift) was difficult this round — a very common pattern, since WCST is specifically designed to be hard to game.
recommendations: After a run of wrong answers, deliberately try a different attribute (color, then shape, then count) rather than repeating your last guess
When you notice several sorts in a row going wrong after previously doing well, that's the signal the rule just shifted — treat it as new information, not bad luck
Retake later — this measure is sensitive to mental fatigue and rushing

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Found the rule reliably at least once, but shifts cost several extra wrong sorts before adapting.
recommendations: Practice noticing a shift faster — 2-3 wrong sorts in a row after previously being consistent is a strong shift signal
Consciously test a *different* attribute after a few wrong sorts rather than persisting with what worked before

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: Adapts to rule shifts reasonably quickly, with occasional perseveration right after a shift.
recommendations: Push for faster shift detection — aim to catch a shift within 1-2 wrong sorts
Notice which of the three rule types (color/shape/number) you personally find hardest to switch to

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: Detects rule shifts quickly and rarely perseverates on an outdated rule.
recommendations: This is a strong, genuine set-shifting result — a real asset in fast-changing work environments
Notice how this compares to your Executive Function Profiling 'Shift' scale, if you've taken it

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Near-optimal set-shifting — categories completed quickly with minimal perseverative errors.
recommendations: This is an elite cognitive-flexibility result on one of neuropsychology's most established measures
Consider how this shows up as an advantage in ambiguous or frequently-changing work

questions.questionText: Sort each card under the key card you believe it matches.
